vectorTools.title: Vector tools
vectorTools.description: Run common vector geometry operations on your GeoJSON layers.

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.description: Create a buffer polygon around each feature by a fixed distance

side.label: Buffer side
side.description: Outside grows each feature, Inside shrinks it, and Both keeps the zone within the distance on either side of its boundary. Inside needs polygon input — a point or line has no interior to buffer into.

dissolve.label: Dissolve result
dissolve.description: Merge the buffers into one feature and dissolve the overlaps between them. The merged shape belongs to no input feature, so attributes are dropped; to dissolve by an attribute, run the Dissolve tool on the result.

centroids.name: Centroids
centroids.description: Compute the centroid point of each feature

convex-hull.name: Convex hull
convex-hull.description: Compute the convex hull enclosing all features

dissolve.name: Dissolve
dissolve.description: Merge polygon features into a single geometry, optionally grouped by a field

field.label: Dissolve field (optional)
field.description: Property name to group features by before dissolving

bounding-box.name: Bounding box
bounding-box.description: Compute the rectangular envelope of all features

simplify.name: Simplify
simplify.description: Reduce the number of vertices using Douglas-Peucker

clip.name: Clip
clip.description: Clip the input layer to the area covered by an overlay layer (keeps input attributes)

intersection.name: Intersection
intersection.description: Keep only the areas where both polygon layers overlap

difference.name: Difference
difference.description: Remove the overlay layer's area from the input layer

union.name: Union
union.description: Merge two polygon layers into a single combined geometry

spatial-join.name: Spatial join
spatial-join.description: Attach attributes from a join layer to each input feature based on a spatial relationship

attribute-join.name: Attribute join
attribute-join.description: Attach attributes from a join layer (a table) onto each input feature where a key field matches, without using geometry. One-to-one: the first matching join row wins.

overlay.label: Join layer (table)
overlay.description: The layer whose attributes are brought over. Its geometry is ignored.

fields.label: Fields to bring over (optional)
fields.description: Comma-separated join fields to copy. Leave blank to bring over every join field except the key.

select-by-value.name: Select by value
select-by-value.description: Extract features whose attribute value matches a condition into a new layer

value.label: Value
value.description: Compared as a number when both sides are numeric.

select-by-location.name: Select by location
select-by-location.description: Extract features by their spatial relationship to a second layer into a new layer

random-extract.name: Random extract
random-extract.description: Extract a random subset of features into a new layer, sized by a feature count or a percentage of the input.

count.label: Number of features
count.description: Clamped to the number of input features when larger.

reproject.name: Reproject
reproject.description: Reinterpret a layer's coordinates as a source CRS and transform them to WGS84 so they display in the correct location. Requires the Sidecar or Python engine.

source_crs.label: Source CRS
source_crs.description: The CRS the layer's coordinates are really in (e.g. EPSG:3857). The result is transformed to WGS84 (EPSG:4326).

explode.name: Explode
explode.description: Split multipart geometries into single-part features (one feature per part), keeping each parent's attributes

aggregate.name: Aggregate by attribute
aggregate.description: Dissolve features that share an attribute value into one geometry per group, with a summary statistic

stat_field.label: Statistic field
stat_field.description: Numeric field summarized by the statistic above.

smooth.name: Smooth
smooth.description: Round the corners of line and polygon features with Chaikin's algorithm (adds vertices), distinct from Simplify's vertex reduction. Z/elevation is preserved; points pass through unchanged.

iterations.label: Iterations
iterations.description: More iterations give a smoother result (1-10).

extract-vertices.name: Extract vertices
extract-vertices.description: Convert every vertex of the input features into a point, keeping the original attributes plus vertex_index and part_index columns (same-named source attributes are overwritten)

points-along-geometry.name: Points along geometry
points-along-geometry.description: Generate points at a fixed distance interval along lines and polygon boundaries; the first and last vertices are always included. Each point gets a distance column (a same-named source attribute is overwritten)

grid.name: Regular grid
grid.description: Generate a regular rectangular grid (fishnet) of cells over an extent. Source: the current map view, a layer's extent, or a manual bounding box.

cell_height.label: Cell height (degrees)
cell_height.description: Leave blank to match the cell width.

voronoi.name: Voronoi / Delaunay
voronoi.description: Build a Voronoi diagram (one polygon per point, clipped to the points' extent) or a Delaunay triangulation from a point layer.

cell-sectors.name: Cell-site coverage
cell-sectors.description: Build antenna sector/wedge polygons from point sites using azimuth, radius and beamwidth (read from attribute fields or fixed values). Beamwidth is clamped to 360° (a full circle); the recorded beamwidth reflects the clamped value. Useful for cell-tower coverage, like QGIS Shape Tools.

azimuthField.label: Azimuth field (°)
azimuthField.description: Direction the sector faces, in degrees clockwise from north. Falls back to the fixed azimuth when blank or non-numeric.

radiusField.label: Radius field
radiusField.description: Coverage radius. Falls back to the fixed radius when blank or non-numeric.

beamwidthField.label: Beamwidth field (°)
beamwidthField.description: Angular width of the sector, clamped to 360° (a full circle). Falls back to the fixed beamwidth when blank or non-numeric.

decode-polyline.name: Decode polyline
decode-polyline.description: Decode encoded polyline strings from an attribute field into a LineString vector layer

field.label: Polyline field
field.description: Attribute field containing the encoded polyline string

encode-polyline.name: Encode line to polyline
encode-polyline.description: Encode LineString and MultiLineString geometries into an encoded polyline attribute string

targetField.label: Output field name
targetField.description: Name of the attribute column to store encoded polylines (default: polyline)

dggs-grid.name: DGGS Generator
dggs-grid.description: Fill an area with DGGS cells (H3, S2, A5, DGGRID, DGGAL). Source: a layer's geometry, a layer's extent, the current map view, or a manual bounding box.

dggridType.label: DGGRID type
dggridType.description: Grid configuration passed to duck_dggs as dggs_params (ISEA/FULLER × aperture × topology).

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.description: Range depends on DGGS type. Leave blank to auto-pick from the area.

compactCells.label: Compact cells
compactCells.description: Merge complete sets of sibling cells into coarser parents (fewer features, mixed resolutions).

fixAntimeridian.label: Fix antimeridian
fixAntimeridian.description: Unwrap cell rings that cross ±180° longitude.

dggs-bin.name: DGGS Binning
dggs-bin.description: Aggregate a point layer into DGGS cells (count, or sum/mean/min/max of a numeric field).

dggridType.label: DGGRID type
dggridType.description: Grid configuration passed to duck_dggs as dggs_params (ISEA/FULLER × aperture × topology).

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.description: Range depends on DGGS type. Leave blank to auto-pick from the area.

fixAntimeridian.label: Fix antimeridian
fixAntimeridian.description: Unwrap cell rings that cross ±180° longitude.

dggs-compact.name: DGGS Compact
dggs-compact.description: Compact DGGS polygon cells, or expand them to a uniform resolution (H3, S2, A5, DGGAL). Input must be a cell layer with an ID property.

layer.label: Input DGGS layer
layer.description: Polygon cell layer from DGGS Generator / Binning (or equivalent).

cellField.label: Cell ID field
cellField.description: Defaults to h3, a5, s2, or dggal for the selected type when left blank.

resolution.label: Target resolution
resolution.description: Resolution to expand to. Must be at least as fine as the input cells.

fixAntimeridian.label: Fix antimeridian
fixAntimeridian.description: Unwrap cell rings that cross ±180° longitude.

trajectory-speed.name: Trajectory speed
trajectory-speed.description: Order points by time (per target) and connect consecutive fixes into segments carrying distance, duration and speed. Like QGIS TrajecTools.

timeField.label: Time field
timeField.description: Timestamp per fix: an ISO date/time string or an epoch (seconds or milliseconds).

idField.label: Target id field
idField.description: Splits the points into separate trajectories. Leave blank to treat all points as one target.

detect-stops.name: Detect stops
detect-stops.description: Find places where a target dwells: runs of consecutive fixes that stay within a distance (absorbing GPS scatter) for at least a minimum duration. Outputs one point per stop. Like QGIS TrajecTools.

timeField.label: Time field
timeField.description: Timestamp per fix: an ISO date/time string or an epoch (seconds or milliseconds).

idField.label: Target id field
idField.description: Detects stops per target. Leave blank to treat all points as one target.

maxDistance.label: Max distance
maxDistance.description: Every fix in a stop must be within this distance of the stop's first fix (so a stop can span up to twice this value). Set it to your GPS scatter radius.

minDuration.label: Min duration (s)
minDuration.description: A dwell shorter than this is not reported as a stop.

space-time-proximity.name: Space-time proximity
space-time-proximity.description: Find pairs of points close in both space and time — e.g. two targets meeting. Outputs a line connecting each qualifying pair, carrying the distance and time gap.

timeField.label: Time field
timeField.description: Timestamp per point: an ISO date/time string or an epoch (seconds or milliseconds).

idField.label: Target id field
idField.description: When set, only points with DIFFERENT id values are paired (encounters between distinct targets). Leave blank to consider every pair.

merge-layers.name: Merge layers
merge-layers.description: Combine several vector layers into one, uniting their attribute schemas (missing attributes become null)

layers.label: Input layers
layers.description: Select two or more layers; they are concatenated in the order shown

addSourceField.label: Add source layer field
addSourceField.description: Record each output feature's originating layer name

sourceFieldName.label: Source field name
sourceFieldName.description: Name of the field that stores the originating layer name

check-validity.name: Check validity
check-validity.description: Find features with invalid geometry (GEOS rules: self-intersecting rings, holes outside shells, ...) and mark them on the map

fix-geometries.name: Fix geometries
fix-geometries.description: Repair invalid geometries with ST_MakeValid (GEOS); valid features pass through untouched

check-topology-rules.name: Check topology rules
check-topology-rules.description: Validate the layer against topology rules (overlaps, gaps, self-intersections, dangles) and mark each violation on the map

rulePointCovered.label: Points must be covered by a line

ruleEndpointSnap.label: Line endpoints must connect within tolerance

snapTolerance.label: Snap tolerance
snapTolerance.description: For the endpoint rule: how far apart (in layer coordinate units — degrees for WGS84) two line ends may be and still count as connected.

fix-topology.name: Fix topology
fix-topology.description: Automatically repair topology violations: snap nearly-connected line endpoints, fix dangles, and project points onto lines. Free ends with nothing nearby are left unchanged.

ruleDangles.label: Repair dangles (snap or project onto nearby geometry)

rulePointCovered.label: Project points onto the nearest line

snapTolerance.label: Snap tolerance
snapTolerance.description: How far (in layer coordinate units — degrees for WGS84) geometry may move to connect.

dryRun.label: Preview only (dry run)
dryRun.description: Report the fixes that would be applied without creating a repaired layer.

isochrone.name: Isochrone / service area
isochrone.description: Travel-time or travel-distance reachability polygons from each point in a layer

contours.label: Contours
contours.description: Comma-separated values (minutes for time, km for distance)

od-matrix.name: OD cost matrix
od-matrix.description: Travel time and distance between every origin and destination point, as connecting lines

sequential-route.name: Sequential route (directions)
sequential-route.description: Connect points in sequence along the road network into a route. Each point is snapped to the nearest road, so off-road coordinates (cell sites, sensors) still route. Order follows the chosen field (e.g. a timestamp) or the layer's feature order.

order_field.label: Order by field (optional)
order_field.description: Sort points by this field (numbers or timestamps) before routing. Leave empty to use the layer's feature order.

global-morans-i.name: Global Moran's I
global-morans-i.description: Measure overall spatial autocorrelation of a numeric attribute across the whole layer.

weightsType.label: Spatial weights
weightsType.description: How neighbors are defined for each feature.

permutations.label: Permutations
permutations.description: Random permutations for the pseudo p-value.

local-morans-i.name: Local Moran's I (LISA)
local-morans-i.description: Per-feature clusters and outliers (High-High, Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High) with pseudo significance.

weightsType.label: Spatial weights
weightsType.description: How neighbors are defined for each feature.

permutations.label: Permutations
permutations.description: Random permutations for the pseudo p-value.

getis-ord-gi.name: Getis-Ord Gi* hotspots
getis-ord-gi.description: Identify statistically significant hot spots and cold spots of a numeric attribute.

weightsType.label: Spatial weights
weightsType.description: How neighbors are defined for each feature.

average-nearest-neighbor.name: Average nearest neighbor
average-nearest-neighbor.description: Test whether points are clustered, dispersed, or randomly distributed (ANN ratio + z-score).

kernel-density.name: Kernel density (heatmap)
kernel-density.description: Estimate a density surface from points as a grid of cells, using a quartic kernel.

weightField.label: Weight field (optional)
weightField.description: Numeric field weighting each point; blank = equal weight.

emerging-hot-spot.name: Emerging Hot Spot (space-time cube)
emerging-hot-spot.description: Build a space-time cube from timestamped points (a fishnet grid × equal time steps) and classify each cell as a new, intensifying, persistent, diminishing, sporadic, oscillating, or historical hot/cold spot. Runs Getis-Ord Gi* per time slice, then a Mann-Kendall trend test on each cell's Gi* series. Client-side, like ArcGIS Emerging Hot Spot Analysis.

timeField.label: Time field
timeField.description: Timestamp per point: an ISO date/time string or an epoch (seconds or milliseconds).

cellSize.label: Cell size (km)
cellSize.description: Edge length of each square spatial bin, in kilometres.

weightField.label: Weight field (optional)
weightField.description: Numeric field summed per space-time bin instead of counting points; blank = count points.

confidence.label: Confidence level
confidence.description: Significance threshold for a bin to count as a hot/cold spot and for the trend.

composite-score.name: Composite score (suitability index)
composite-score.description: Normalize, weight, and combine several numeric fields into a single 0-100 index, then style the layer by it.

fields.label: Fields and weights
fields.description: Two or more numeric fields. Each gets a normalization, a relative weight, and the end of its range that scores well.

aggregation.label: Aggregation
aggregation.description: The geometric mean lets a weak field pull the score down: a strong field cannot fully compensate for it.

nullHandling.label: Features missing a value
nullHandling.description: There is no safe default: dropping and renormalizing produce different maps, so choose which one this index means.

options.drop: Drop the feature from the result
options.renormalize: Renormalize weights over the fields it has

scoreField.label: Score field name
scoreField.description: Name of the numeric column the score is written to.

keepComponents.label: Keep normalized components
keepComponents.description: Write each field's normalized value as its own column, so the score can be audited instead of taken on trust.

hillshade.name: Hillshade
hillshade.description: Compute a shaded-relief (hillshade) raster from an elevation model.

slope.name: Slope
slope.description: Compute slope (steepness) from an elevation model.

aspect.name: Aspect
aspect.description: Compute aspect (compass direction of the steepest slope) from an elevation model.

reproject.name: Reproject
reproject.description: Warp a raster to a different coordinate reference system.

dst_crs.label: Target CRS
dst_crs.description: An authority code such as EPSG:3857 or EPSG:4326.

resample.name: Resample
resample.description: Resample a raster to a different pixel size (resolution).

resolution.label: Target pixel size
resolution.description: Output pixel size in the raster's CRS units.

clip-extent.name: Clip by extent
clip-extent.description: Crop a raster to a bounding box (in the raster's CRS).

clip-mask.name: Clip by mask layer
clip-mask.description: Clip a raster to the geometries of a vector mask file.

mask_path.label: Mask layer
mask_path.description: A GeoJSON file whose geometries define the clip region. It is reprojected to the raster's CRS automatically (a GeoJSON with no CRS is assumed to be WGS84).

polygonize.name: Polygonize
polygonize.description: Convert a raster band into vector polygons grouped by pixel value.

contour.name: Contour
contour.description: Generate contour lines from an elevation model.

interval.label: Interval
interval.description: Elevation difference between successive contour lines.

interpolate.name: Interpolation (IDW / Kriging)
interpolate.description: Interpolate a point layer's numeric attribute into a continuous raster surface using inverse distance weighting or ordinary kriging.

field.label: Value field
field.description: Name of the numeric point attribute to interpolate (e.g. elevation, temperature).

resolution.label: Output pixel size
resolution.description: Cell size in the layer's CRS units (degrees for WGS84). The grid covers the points' extent.

power.label: IDW power
power.description: Higher values give nearby points more influence.

variogram_model.label: Variogram model
variogram_model.description: Theoretical model fitted to the empirical semivariogram. Kriging is capped at 1500 points.

zonal.name: Zonal statistics
zonal.description: Summarize raster values within each polygon of a vector layer (count, min, max, mean, sum, std, median).

zones_path.label: Zones layer
zones_path.description: A GeoJSON polygon layer defining the zones. It is reprojected to the raster's CRS automatically (a GeoJSON with no CRS is assumed to be WGS84).

prefix.label: Field prefix
prefix.description: Prepended to each statistic field name (e.g. 'dem_' → 'dem_mean'). Leave blank for bare 'mean', 'min', …

raster-calc.name: Raster calculator
raster-calc.description: Evaluate a NumPy band-math expression. Reference band 1 of each input as A, B, C and specific bands as A1, A2, …; e.g. NDVI is (A2 - A1) / (A2 + A1).

expression.label: Expression
expression.description: A NumPy expression over A, B, C (and A1, A2, …). Functions: where, log, exp, sqrt, abs, clip, minimum, maximum, sin, cos, tan.

b_path.label: Raster B (optional)
b_path.description: A second raster, referenced as B / B1, B2, …. Must match A's dimensions.

c_path.label: Raster C (optional)
c_path.description: A third raster, referenced as C / C1, C2, …. Must match A's dimensions.

spectral-index.name: Spectral index
spectral-index.description: Compute a named spectral index (NDVI, NDWI, EVI, …) from a multiband raster. Pick a sensor preset for the band layout, or set band numbers manually with the Custom sensor.

sensor.label: Sensor / band layout
sensor.description: Preset band numbers for common sensors. Choose Custom to map bands by hand for a differently stacked GeoTIFF.

options.sentinel2: Sentinel-2 (B2, B3, B4, B8, B11, B12)

L.label: Soil factor (L)
L.description: SAVI soil-brightness correction (0 dense cover → 1 bare soil).

scale.label: Reflectance scale
scale.description: Multiplier converting pixel values to reflectance (0–1). Leave at 1 for normalized-difference indices; set it for EVI/SAVI on integer-DN imagery (e.g. 0.0001 for Sentinel-2 L2A).

reclassify.name: Reclassify
reclassify.description: Remap value ranges to new class values using a rule table.

table.label: Rules
table.description: Comma- or newline-separated 'min:max:newvalue' rules, e.g. '0:10:1, 10:20:2, 20:max:3'. Ranges are half-open [min, max); blank/min/max mean ±∞.

mosaic.name: Mosaic / merge
mosaic.description: Combine up to five rasters (sharing a CRS) into a single raster covering their union.

method.label: Overlap method
method.description: Which value wins where inputs overlap.

focal.name: Focal statistics
focal.description: Apply a moving-window (neighbourhood) statistic to a raster band.

size.label: Window size
size.description: Odd neighbourhood size in pixels (3 = 3×3). Capped at 25.

atmosphere.haloExtentHint: How far the atmospheric glow reaches past the globe. Lower keeps data tight to the surface; higher gives a wide, airy halo.
atmosphere.globeOnly: Atmospheric effects are only available when Globe view is enabled.

sun.title: Sun
sun.localTimeNote: Times shown in your computer's time zone.

routeAnimation.title: Route Animation
routeAnimation.noLineLayers: No line layers in the project
routeAnimation.videoError: Could not record the animation. Please try again.
routeAnimation.videoUnsupported: Video recording isn't supported in this browser.

errors.notActive: The route animation is not active.
errors.selectLineLayer: Select a line layer with length before recording.
errors.encoderTimeout: Recording timed out waiting for the encoder.

flightSim.title: Flight Simulator
flightSim.heading: Heading
flightSim.bankCameraMapbox: Mapbox GL has no camera roll, so the horizon stays level here. The aircraft still banks and turns.
flightSim.help: Arrows or A/D steer · W/S or Page Up/Down throttle · Space levels the wings · Esc exits.

setView.title: Set View
setView.description: Move the map to an exact camera.
setView.smartPasteInfo: Type or paste a full coordinate string in DD, DMS, or DDM, or a grid reference in MGRS, USNG, or UTM, then run Process input. GeoLibre detects the format and fills the longitude and latitude fields below. Adjust zoom, pitch, and bearing separately before going.
setView.smartPasteInvalid: Could not read those coordinates. Enter a full longitude and latitude in DD, DMS, or DDM, for example 51.5074, -0.1278, or a grid reference such as 18SUJ2337106519 (MGRS), 18S UJ 23371 06519 (USNG), or 18S 323394 4307395 (UTM). conversion.rasterToPmtilesDesc: Render a raster into a single PMTiles archive of Web Mercator PNG tiles, ready for cloud-native serving. One band is rendered through a colormap, so multi-band imagery is not drawn in true colour. Runs entirely in WebAssembly, so it needs no sidecar on either the web or desktop app.
conversion.cogBrowserNote: In the browser, 8-bit rasters keep their type and everything else (Int16 DEMs, Float64, …) is written as Float32. The desktop app preserves the original type.
conversion.notAGeoTiffRasterOnly: This file is not a readable GeoTIFF. Raster to PMTiles reads GeoTIFF only, on both the web and desktop app.
conversion.bandError: Band must be a positive whole number.
conversion.bandOutOfRange: Band {{band}} does not exist; this raster has {{bands}} band(s).
conversion.runsInBrowserVectorEngines: Conversion runs in your browser with DuckDB-WASM, or geolibre-wasm for FlatGeobuf output.
conversion.vectorToVectorDesc: Convert between any vector formats DuckDB's spatial extension supports. The input and output formats are detected from the file extensions. The desktop app writes any format (FlatGeobuf, GeoPackage, Shapefile, KML, GML, …); the browser writes GeoJSON, CSV, GeoParquet, GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf, and Shapefile.
conversion.vectorToGeoparquetDesc: Convert a vector dataset to a Hilbert-sorted, compressed GeoParquet file optimized for cloud-native range requests.
conversion.vectorToFlatgeobufDesc: Convert a vector dataset to a Hilbert-sorted FlatGeobuf with a packed spatial index for fast cloud-native access.
conversion.vectorToShapefileDesc: Convert a vector dataset to a zipped ESRI Shapefile (.shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj). Field names are truncated to 10 characters.
conversion.vectorToGeopackageDesc: Convert a vector dataset to a GeoPackage (.gpkg) for sharing with QGIS, ArcGIS, and other GIS tools.
conversion.csvToGeoparquetDesc: Build point geometries from longitude/latitude columns and write a Hilbert-sorted, compressed GeoParquet.
conversion.vectorToPmtilesDesc: Tile a vector dataset into a single PMTiles archive of vector tiles, ready for cloud-native serving.
conversion.rasterToCogDesc: Convert a raster dataset to a valid, compressed Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF with internal tiling and overviews.
conversion.shapefileSidecarHint: For Shapefiles, select the .shp together with its .dbf, .shx, and .prj files.

item.embedVectorDesc: This project has {{count}} local vector layer(s) loaded from your computer. The browser cannot re-read them when the project is reopened, so their data must be embedded in the project file to be restored. Embedding adds about {{size}} to the file.
item.embedVectorDescDesktop: This project has {{count}} local vector layer(s) loaded from your computer. Embed their data to make the project self-contained (adds about {{size}}), or save file references that reload from disk when the project is reopened. References keep the file small but break if a source file is later moved or deleted.
item.embedVectorDescMas: This project has {{count}} local vector layer(s) loaded from your computer. The Mac App Store sandbox cannot retain access to those files after GeoLibre closes, so their data must be embedded in the project file to be restored. Embedding adds about {{size}} to the file.
item.embedVectorLargeWarning: Embedding about {{size}} makes a very large project file. Reopening it may be slow or fail outright, because every feature has to be parsed and held in memory at once. For data this size, convert the layers to PMTiles or FlatGeobuf and add them as remote layers instead of embedding them.

item.directionsNoticeTitle: Directions uses a public routing server
item.directionsNoticeDesc: Turning on Directions sends the waypoints you place to the public OSRM demo server (router.project-osrm.org) to calculate routes — your coordinates leave your device for those requests. The demo server is rate-limited and supports driving only.
item.reverseGeocodeTooltip: Click the map to look up an address. The clicked coordinates are sent to the configured geocoding provider (public Nominatim by default; change it in Settings → Geocoding).
item.reverseGeocodeNoticeTitle: Reverse Geocode uses an external service
item.reverseGeocodeNoticeDesc: Turning on Reverse Geocode sends the coordinates of each point you click to the configured geocoding provider (the public Nominatim service by default) to resolve an address — your coordinates leave your device for those requests. You can choose a different provider in Settings → Geocoding.
item.networkNoticeTitle: Network analysis uses an external routing server
item.networkNoticeDesc: Running a Network analysis tool sends the coordinates of your input points to a routing server to compute isochrones, cost matrices, and routes.
item.networkNoticePrivacy: Your input coordinates leave this device and are sent to the public Valhalla server at valhalla1.openstreetmap.de. Press Cancel if your project is bound by data privacy or data-sovereignty rules.
item.networkNoticePrivacyCustom: Your input coordinates leave this device and are sent to the configured routing server ({{endpoint}}). Press Cancel if your project is bound by data privacy or data-sovereignty rules.
item.networkNoticePerformance: The public server is free but rate-limited, so large batches of points may be throttled or fail. For heavy use, run your own Valhalla server and enter its URL in the tool's "Routing server (Valhalla)" field (or set VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINT in Settings → Environment Variables to make it the default).
item.largeOsmPbfDesc: This file is about {{sizeMb}} MB. Parsing it converts every feature to GeoJSON in memory, which can be slow and may use a lot of memory in the browser. Continue?
item.largeVectorDesc: {{name}} has about {{count}} features. Loading it converts every feature to GeoJSON in memory and may slow down or freeze the app. Continue?
item.addOsmPbfLayerDesc: Load an OpenStreetMap .osm.pbf file. It is parsed in your browser and split into separate point, line, and polygon layers.
item.osmPbfUrlHint: Remote URLs load in the desktop app; in the browser the server must allow cross-origin requests (CORS).
item.loadingOsmPbfDesc: Parsing the file and converting features to GeoJSON. This runs in the background and may take a moment for large extracts.
item.loadingOsmPbfProgress: Converting features to GeoJSON… {{processed}} of {{total}} OSM entities processed.
item.pointerElevationNoticeTitle: Elevation uses a public elevation service
item.pointerElevationNoticeDesc: The status bar's elevation readout is resolved from the map's own 3D terrain when that is enabled, which sends nothing anywhere. Without 3D terrain it falls back to the public Open-Meteo elevation API, and the coordinates under your pointer leave your device for those requests.

description.postgis: Run PostGIS SQL against loaded layers. The PostGIS extension is loaded, so ST_* functions are available. The first run loads a ~19 MB database engine.
description.duckdb: Run DuckDB SQL against loaded layers, files, and URLs. The spatial extension is loaded, so ST_* functions are available. Cloud URLs (s3://, gs://, az://) are supported for public data.
description.sedona: Run Apache Sedona spatial SQL against loaded layers. Runs in-browser via CereusDB (a WebAssembly build of SedonaDB); on desktop it uses the SedonaDB sidecar when the optional sedona extra is installed. ST_* functions are available.
